reviews.text: Use the mobile app to book your appointment. It saves a lot of time. Your pet will thank you for it 😊

The initial intake process was fairly smooth. I got to the truck super early as I've read that the line does get pretty long. I was there at the opening time listed but I waited about 40 mins for staff to arrive. The staff were more than helpful, respectful, and caring.

I can't speak on Garo's professionalism because he was more than professional and receptive to my concerns and questions. Garo explained to me in detail what was going on and how he was treating my cat. I was a bit hesitant due to the reviews I had seen but, I was in dire need of getting my cat assistance as his condition was crucial.
I appreciated that Garo allowed me to visit my cat and check up on him. My cat was relocated to a house to continue his treatment. It is not aesthetically pleasing but this is a low cost vet so resources are limited and they're doing the best they can with what's available to them.
The experience was good however my cat had a urinary blockage and as I picked him up to take him home, he was blocked again. Garo insisted on putting the catheter back in. I was a bit concerned because it's not a pleasant experience and Garo didn't think it was necessary to do sedation. Garo told me to hold my cat as he tried to put the catheter back in but my cat was YOWLING and resisting it. It seemed like a lot of stress on my cat who was already dealing with a stressful situation. There are certain things pet owners shouldn't have to experience and I think that's one of them. I took my cat and was able to get him the help he needed.
The location I picked my cat up at isn't the most aesthetically pleasing but Garo DID unblock my cat and I am grateful for that.
It's important to note that you get what you pay for and Garo doesn't have access to resources that many vets do and he's doing the best he can. It's clear that Garo does care about the animals. I was just concerned about the lack of medication to ease my cat's pain and I think the attempt to put the catheter back in, solidified that I wanted to take my cat elsewhere. Other than that, I felt that my cat was taken care of and that Garo and his team were very informative and kept me updated.

This outfit ostensibly exists to provide low-cost veterinary care to rescues and low-income pet owners. This is a noble mission, and for all I know, they do some good in fulfilling it. However, if you are simply looking for a cut-rate service, do not expect to get it on time or with professionalism.

We waited five hours with my dog and cat to get basic blood work done. They refused to do the cat because she tried to bite them. "Duh, you need to immobilize the pet." I offered to help, and they refused. They did the dog, then called to give me very vague results over the phone and refused to give me actual numbers, despite confirming on the phone that they had them in front of them. "The person who uploads the results to the app" (what app? No info) is "on vacation", and we are not going to get those results for more than three weeks.

My dog is in a serious health crisis, and we are going to have to get the testing redone to manage that. We wasted hundreds of dollars' worth of our time, got an incredibly unprofessional and rude attitude from the staff, and were treated with nothing but contempt throughout. They then had the nerve to claim they were banning us, as if we would ever use them again, for threatening to take them to small claims court if they did not deliver.

If you have no other choice, then use them, but if you can afford to go to a real vet, definitely do that. Unless you want to be treated with absolute contempt and put your pet's health at risk.

Every review about the attitude is true. For over 10 years, every time I’ve called, I’ve dreaded it because of the nasty, condescending way this person speaks to people. If you’re confused about the website, he’ll rant about how the site is perfectly fine. If you call about something your dog has been seen for before, he’ll tell you he doesn’t care about that and that the dog needs a new checkup.

Just yesterday, I called to get an estimate for my dog’s routine yearly sonogram and to have her eyes and ears checked because her allergies have always caused recurring infections. He told me they would need to examine her to determine whether she had an eye issue. I explained that, aside from her routine infections, she already has a serious eye condition and sees an eye specialist. Instead of listening, he proceeded to recommend that I take her to a specialist.

I told him that’s exactly what I had just said—that she had already seen a specialist and received a diagnosis. That’s how I know she is blind and that the damage is irreparable. I explained that I didn’t have the exact name of the diagnosis in front of me but would find the paperwork. At that point, he went on such a rant that when I tried to explain again that she was already diagnosed and seeing the very specialist he was recommending, he yelled, “Are you going to let me speak?!”

So I let him speak. Then, before I could even get back to the simple reason I called in the first place—to ask how much her routine eye and ear checkup would cost—he cut me off and said, “I’m done talking to you because you don’t listen.”

The irony is unbelievable.

And before he comes on here to defend himself, as I’ve seen him do, I want to make one thing clear: this has been my experience for over 10 years. This organization provides an important service for people who may not be able to afford regular veterinary care, which makes the condescending, disgusting attitude even more frustrating. Helping people on a budget doesn’t give you the right to treat them as if they should be grateful enough to tolerate being spoken to any kind of way.

On May 22nd, my mother brought her cat in because she had a black round wound on her body that was draining fluid. What started as a single spot had already begun spreading across her belly. We were extremely worried and sought professional help immediately.

The veterinarian told us it was “dead skin” and recommended hospitalization and testing. We trusted his judgment and agreed to everything he recommended because we believed our cat would receive proper care and treatment. Over the next several days, we were repeatedly told that everything was okay and that there was nothing to worry about.

When it was time to pick her up, we were shocked. Our cat had been hospitalized in a house. We expected a clean veterinary facility equipped to properly monitor and care for animals requiring hospitalization. Instead, we arrived at a house, and the moment we walked into the porch area, the smell was absolutely horrible. The odor was overwhelming and immediately raised concerns about the cleanliness and sanitary conditions where animals were being kept.

Despite being repeatedly reassured that our cat was doing well, she passed away only five days after we brought her home.

We spent approximately $1,500 on hospitalization, tests, and treatment, only to lose our beloved cat less than a week later. The emotional devastation is difficult to put into words. She wasn’t just a pet she was a member of our family.

What makes this experience even more painful is the lack of answers. We were continually told everything was fine. If everything was truly fine, why did she die only days later? If the condition was serious enough to require hospitalization, why were we not given a clearer understanding of the severity of her illness?

We understand that veterinarians cannot save every animal. However, pet owners deserve honesty, transparency, professionalism, and confidence that their pets are receiving proper care in a clean and sanitary environment.

Instead, we were left with a $1,500 bill, a broken heart, and more questions than answers. Losing a beloved pet is painful enough. Being repeatedly reassured that everything is okay, only to watch your pet die days later, makes that pain even worse.

Our family will never forget this experience. We trusted them with the life of a family member, and that trust was shattered.

My kitten was not doing well and was throwing up for almost 2 days. I called, and the man who answered the phone (I forgot his name) was really helpful and told me to bring him in right away. The wait was a little long, but there was a line, and honestly for how many people were there, I feel like the wait time was reasonable.

It ended up being an emergency surgery, and they did it right away, which I appreciated so much. The cost compared to other places was actually good, and they offer payment plan options which made it so much easier for me to say yes immediately.

Because it’s a low-cost vet, the updates weren’t the best. I was calling every day to check on him because I was extremely anxious the whole time, but the staff member I spoke with was always patient with me and never rude. Leaving my little baby there for 2 and a half days felt like eternity. It’s been almost a week now and he’s doing so much better and hasn’t thrown up since.

The only thing I didn’t really like was that he smelled really bad when we picked him up. I think the area he stayed in could’ve been cleaner. But at the same time, I understand they see so many animals every day.

Other than that, would I recommend them? Yes.

Heard about the tragedy that occurred and I am in disbelief. Had taken my cat Rupert for a cystotomy 2 months ago and they were very quick in giving me an appointment 2 days from scheduling. The owner assisted me and answered all my questions. He was never once rude and I knew to keep my questions short because I know he's helping save and treat countless animal lives. He wrote down all the instructions I needed to follow clearly. He even gave me samples of some of the different urinary prescription food the cat would need to eat for the rest of his life to prevent any stone reoccurrence. Showed me the bladder stones removed initially thought to be 3 but was 4 and explained why some cats get them, showed me the difference between struvite and oxalate stones and how to prevent them. The price is the most affordable of any clinics I've been to or researched in NY and even in outer states.  The wait time is understandable as he is working with and treating many pets. They would work even past midnight sometimes to make sure all their customers are attended to. We waited in the freezing cold today, waiting for anyone to show up. One person was on line from 6am, another 730, I was there since 8am. It was 11 degrees outside. They did not open the clinic at 9am as it says they do all over the website. Eventually some people came, two hours late, at 11am, to tell us that services are indefinitely suspended because unfortunately the vet passed away the night before. Sincerely, my condolences to the vet and his/her family. But here is my issue. Of course there are unavoidable emergencies and sometimes businesses must close. Understood. However, communication is in the business owner's control. They could have done anything, updated their voicemail to say they're closed today, left a sign on on truck, sent someone at 9am to tell us they are closed, anything. But instead we were in the freezing cold until 11am. The communication needs to improve. Period. The business owner goes out the way to use hostile language on the website and google reviews, and goes out the way to post news paper clippings all over the truck, so the owner understands the power of communication. Even if you are dealing with an emergency and providing affordable service you can still respect customers and make an effort to communicate to them so they are not waiting around for hours in the freezing cold for no reason. A business owner should be able to understand this. Do better.

By far the rudest vets I’ve ever dealt with. Yes, they’re low cost—but that’s literally the only positive. Everything else is exactly what you’d expect: poor organization, unclear processes, and extremely rude staff who get irritated or even yell at you for asking basic questions about your pet’s care.
Appointments are nearly impossible to get, and even when you supposedly “have one,” they refuse to give an actual date—only vague estimates, even after you’ve already paid and explained that the situation is urgent. There is no transparency or accountability whatsoever. Asking for clarification is treated like a personal offense, and instead of explaining next steps, the vet talks down to you as if you’re stupid for advocating for your own pet.
On top of that, services are done in a van, which felt rushed and unsanitary—absolutely not something I’m comfortable with when it comes to medical care or surgery.

I would strongly recommend paying an extra $30–$50 and going to a place that actually provides professional, humane, and respectful service. There are far better options available. The Humane Society is amazing and I highly recommend them.

Unfortunately, I had to continue with this clinic only because I had already paid before being told that it could take weeks, if not months, for my pet to actually be seen. To make things worse, if you try to cancel, they charge a $50 cancellation fee.

I deeply regret not checking their Google reviews beforehand, especially their defensive and unprofessional replies to criticism—those alone should have been a red flag. Save your time, your sanity, and potentially your pet’s health. I would never recommend this place to anyone, especially if you’re seeking emergency services or basic respect.

I am posting this review after reading the clinic’s public response to my previous review, as several statements made there are factually incorrect.

I did request my dog’s medical records, including the X-ray images, multiple times by phone and email over the course of more than one month. I was never provided with the images or a radiology report, nor was I given clear instructions at the visit on how to access them.

I was never informed that “registration” was required to obtain records, nor was I given access to any diagnostic images through the app. The only information available to me was a generic page without X-ray images or results.

During my most recent call, when I again requested the records I paid for, I was spoken to in an aggressive and hostile manner, interrupted, yelled at, and the call was terminated. Asking questions and requesting medical records should never result in this type of treatment.

I stand by my experience and my original review. Transparency, professionalism, and respectful communication are essential in veterinary care. Unfortunately, that was not my experience here. This matter has now been referred to the appropriate regulatory authorities.

I brought my dog to Low Cost Vet Mobile / Animal Adoption Veterinary Center for diagnostic X-rays. Despite having an appointment, I was required to wait over an hour outside in the cold before being seen, with very little communication from staff.

My dog was taken inside the mobile clinic without any clear explanation of what procedures were being performed. I was later told that the X-ray results would be uploaded to the clinic’s app within one week.

More than one month later, I have still not received the X-ray images or a radiology report. Multiple phone calls and emails requesting my dog’s medical records went unanswered.

When I finally reached someone by phone to request the records, the staff member was verbally aggressive, raised his voice, refused to release the images, and ultimately hung up on me.

Due to the refusal to release medical records, lack of transparency, and unprofessional conduct, I have filed a formal complaint with the New York State Education Department – Office of the Professions.

I strongly caution pet owners to be aware of these issues, especially if you may need access to your pet’s medical records for follow-up care.

I can’t understand how this man has had a business for so many years when he’s so rude and disrespectful. Every single time I’ve been on a call with him he’s disgustingly rude, doesn’t let you talk at all or explain anything, he yells at you, etc. The only reason he keeps getting clients is because people can’t afford regular vets. He should hire someone who actually has manners, compassion and sense of customer support.

I am deeply disappointed and alarmed by the care my dog received from this mobile veterinary clinic.

My dog presented with a clear limp and systemic signs that warranted basic diagnostic testing, including a SNAP 4DX test to rule out tick-borne disease—especially given how common these infections are. No SNAP test was offered or performed. Instead, the veterinarian assumed the issue was orthopedic and even raised the possibility of bone cancer, without first ruling out far more common and treatable causes.

My dog was prescribed carprofen only, which temporarily masked symptoms but did not address the underlying disease. It was later determined that my dog was suffering from anaplasmosis, a tick-borne illness that should have been treated promptly with doxycycline. This delay in diagnosis and proper treatment caused unnecessary suffering and could have led to serious, preventable complications.

Failing to offer a SNAP test in a limping dog—especially before discussing cancer—is a significant lapse in standard veterinary practice. Making assumptions instead of running basic diagnostics is unacceptable.

I trusted this clinic to provide competent, thorough medical care. That trust was misplaced. I would strongly urge pet owners to seek a second opinion elsewhere and ensure proper diagnostics are performed before accepting treatment plans from this provider.
